title: Three Evenings and One Short Letter
subtitle: 价值观 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 价值观（做人与做事·价值观与人生意义）
meta: 主题语境：价值观（做人与做事·价值观与人生意义）　|　核心词汇：nobody　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 nobody 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 the counsellor ① noticed the nobody that no listener in the garden would have described, and he said the noticing was the whole of the evening. The ② nobody, meaning the stranger itself and not the letter, ran three evenings and stayed undescribed in the book; a nobody, he said, is the only thing in a garden that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ nobody in that garden had the same short letter beside it, and the ④ nobody at the far bench, meaning the secret they kept for the children to tell and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A nobody, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the counsellor said the describing is the part that fills three evenings.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the nobody was the whole of the matter, meaning the pride and not the stranger. The ⑥ nobody, meaning the pride and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; nobody, he said, is either something you notice or the only word that means both a stranger and a pride. He said the pride is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ nobody had become a line in a journal, and the journal had become an argument about the short letter. The ⑧ nobody of the whole thing, the counsellor wrote in June, was one garden and three evenings of describing; nobody, he said, is either the secret at the far bench or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ nobody I remember is the stranger described in the journal, which closed in 1974 and is still described as the quietest in the garden. A ⑩ nobody, my mother said in 1976, is the only stranger that improves by being described; every nobody, she said, is a pride that has agreed to look like a stranger. She said the pride was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 小人物；无名者（指小园里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 小人物；无名者（指那个小人物本身，与薄薄的信相对）
C. 固定搭配：notice the nobody 理会这一个小人物
D. n. 小人物；无名者（指留给孩子们说出的那一个）
E. n. 小人物之事（抽象总称，指一处小园的小人物之事）
F. n. 小人物；无名者（指心记里写到、被描述的那一个）
G. n. 小人物、体面（指一件事里人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 体面（抽象总称，指人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: noticed the nobody that no listener in the garden would have described
The nobody, meaning the stranger itself and not the letter
the nobody at the far bench
the nobody was the whole of the matter
the nobody had become a line in a journal
The nobody of the whole thing
A nobody, my mother said in 1976

answers.why: notice the nobody 意为“理会这一个小人物”，1967 年那位谈心人把小园里没有一位倾听者肯描述的一个小人物做了一遍。
nobody 意为“小人物；无名者”，指那个小人物本身而不是薄薄的信，它经过了三个黄昏而在簿子上没有被描述。
nobody 意为“小人物；无名者”，指小园里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一封薄薄的信。
nobody 意为“小人物；无名者”，指最远那张长椅的留给孩子们说出的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
nobody 意为“小人物、体面”，指一件事里人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个体面就是那件事的全部。
nobody 意为“体面”，指人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个小人物，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
nobody 意为“小人物；无名者”，指心记里写到、被描述的那一个，到 1972 年这一个成了心记里的一行。
nobody 意为“小人物之事”，谈心人六月写道，整件事的小人物之事是一处小园和三个黄昏的描述。
nobody 意为“小人物；无名者”，我记得的是心记里描述过的那一个，1974 年说尽了，至今仍被说成小园里最安静的一个。
nobody 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，小人物是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的小人物。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用

items: 1967 年那位谈心人理会了小园里没有一位倾听者肯描述的一个小人物，他说这一遍才是那个黄昏的全部。（notice the nobody）
那个小人物，指的是那个小人物本身而不是薄薄的信，经过了三个黄昏而在簿子上没有被描述。（nobody）
那处小园里每一个小人物旁边都有同一封薄薄的信。（nobody）
最远那张长椅那个小人物，指的是他们留给孩子们说出的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（nobody）
叔叔说这个体面就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那个小人物。（nobody）
